extracted.intended_audience: Florida state agencies, agency rulewriters/heads, regulated parties, and stakeholders affected by Florida administrative rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory procedural and substantive requirements (Fla. Stat. §120.54) for developing, noticing, adopting, modifying, and publishing administrative rules in Florida, including emergency rules, incorporation by reference, small business considerations, hearings, and uniform procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory rulemaking and presumption of feasibility/practicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency statement defined as a rule by s. 120.52 shall be adopted by the rulemaking procedure provided by this section as soon as feasible and practicable. Rulemaking is not a matter of agency discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking is presumed feasible unless agency proves lack of sufficient time to acquire necessary knowledge/experience or related matters are unresolved. Rulemaking is presumed practicable to provide fair notice unless agency proves (a) detail/precision is not reasonable under the circumstances, or (b) questions are so narrow that adjudication is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory implementation timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Legislature enacts an act requiring implementation by agency rules, the rules shall be drafted and formally proposed within the times provided in s. 120.74(4) and (5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow statutory timelines for drafting/proposing rules that implement legislative acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: No delay in statutory implementation unless statute requires
rubrics_metrics.description: No statutory provision shall be delayed in its implementation pending an agency’s adoption of implementing rules unless there is an express statutory provision prohibiting its application until the adoption of implementing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies cannot withhold applying statutory provisions while waiting to adopt rules unless the statute explicitly conditions application on rule adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Least-costly alternative requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In adopting rules, agencies must, among alternative approaches and to the extent allowed by law, choose the alternative that does not impose regulatory costs which could be reduced by adoption of less costly alternatives that substantially accomplish the statutory objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must consider alternatives and prefer less burdensome options that still meet statutory objectives; this is a mandatory constraint in rule selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on inherent authority and rule-based penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: No agency has inherent rulemaking authority, nor authority to establish penalties for violation of a rule unless the Legislature specifically provides that the penalty applies to rules when establishing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may only adopt rules and penalties where statutory authority exists; regulatory power is derivative of legislative grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and retroactivity of rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may adopt rules authorized by law and necessary to implement a statute prior to the statute's effective date, but rules may not be effective until the statute is effective. Agencies may not adopt retroactive rules unless expressly authorized by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule adoption before statutory effective date is allowed, but effectiveness is tethered to statute; retroactive clarifying rules are prohibited absent express statutory authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-subject requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rule adopted shall contain only one subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules must be focused and limited to a single subject to comply with this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and notice of judicially noticed materials
rubrics_metrics.description: In rulemaking proceedings, the agency may recognize any material which may be judicially noticed and may provide that materials so recognized be incorporated into the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before the record is completed, parties must be provided a list of these materials and a reasonable opportunity to examine them and offer written comments or rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule may incorporate material by reference but only as the material exists on the date the rule is adopted; changes in the material are not effective unless the rule is amended to incorporate the changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional incorporation rules: (1) Agency rule that incorporates another rule of that agency automatically incorporates subsequent amendments unless contrary intent is indicated; notices of amendments to incorporated rules must explain effects on referencing rules. (2) For rules adopted after Dec 31, 2010, incorporated material must be submitted in prescribed electronic format and be available via hyperlink for free public access, unless posting would violate federal copyright law—in that case, provide a statement and addresses where material is available. (3) A rule may not be amended by reference only; amendments must set out the amended rule in full. (4) Special cross-agency incorporation (DEP/water management) has additional notification, publication, filing, objection, and effective-date rules. (5) Department of State may adopt requirements for incorporating materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing of published rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule published in the Florida Administrative Code must be indexed by the Department of State within 90 days after the rule is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department of State shall by rule establish procedures for indexing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation limits for agency heads
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency head may delegate the authority to initiate rule development under subsection (2); however, certain rulemaking responsibilities may not be delegated or transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities under specified subparagraphs (e.g., important decision points) may not be delegated; check statutory subparagraph references for non-delegable duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule development notice content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Except when the intended action is repeal, agencies shall provide notice of the development of proposed rules by publication of a notice of rule development in the Florida Administrative Register before providing notice of a proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must indicate the subject area, provide a short plain explanation of purpose/effect, cite legal authority, and include preliminary text if available or state how a person may promptly obtain a copy without cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language/readability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All rules should be drafted in readable language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readable language avoids obscure words, unnecessarily long/complicated constructions, and unnecessary technical or specialized language understood only by particular trades/professions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public workshops for rule development
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may hold public workshops for rule development and must hold workshops in various regions if requested in writing by any affected person, unless the agency head explains in writing why a workshop is unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops must ensure persons preparing the proposed rule are available to explain and respond; workshops may be facilitated/mediated by neutral third persons or use other dispute resolution methods. Notice must be published in the Florida Administrative Register at least 14 days prior and include subject area, agency contact, place, date, and time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiated rulemaking procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may use negotiated rulemaking, using a committee of designated representatives to draft a mutually acceptable proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider negotiated rulemaking for complex or controversial rules; publish notice including listing of representative groups invited; allow applications to participate within 30 days; all meetings must be noticed and open to the public; negotiating committee is chaired by a neutral facilitator; agency decisions about use/selection/approval of participants are not agency action and do not affect rights to challenge proposed rules under s.120.56(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of notice of intended action
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to adoption/amendment/repeal (other than emergency), an agency shall give notice of its intended action setting forth a short plain explanation of the purpose/effect, the full text of the proposed rule or amendment and a summary, reference to rulemaking authority and statutes being implemented or interpreted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must include a summary of the agency’s statement of estimated regulatory costs (if prepared), a statement that persons may provide information or lower-cost alternatives in writing within 21 days, and whether the proposed rule is expected to require legislative ratification. Notice must state procedure for requesting a public hearing and reference date/place of prior rule development notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice publication timing and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall be published in the Florida Administrative Register not less than 28 days prior to the intended action; the proposed rule shall be available for inspection/copying at time of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication at least 28 days before intended action ensures public availability and opportunity to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice mailing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall be mailed to all persons named in the proposed rule and to all persons who, at least 14 days prior to such mailing, have requested advance notice of the agency's proceedings; the agency shall also give such notice as prescribed by rule to classes of persons to whom the intended action is directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must maintain mailing processes to notify named persons and advance-requestors; follow additional rule-prescribed notice for particular classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements with the committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The adopting agency shall file with the committee at least 21 days prior to proposed adoption a copy of each rule it proposes to adopt; any material incorporated by reference; a detailed written statement of facts and circumstances justifying the proposed rule; a copy of any statement of estimated regulatory costs; a statement of extent the proposed rule relates to federal standards; and the notice required by the content provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely and complete filing supports committee review; failure to file required items can lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of estimated regulatory costs (SERC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are encouraged to prepare a statement of estimated regulatory costs of the proposed rule; a SERC is required if the proposed rule will have an adverse impact on small business or is likely to directly or indirectly increase regulatory costs in excess of $200,000 in the aggregate in this state within 1 year after implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare SERC when required; if prepared include its summary in the notice of intended action; provide opportunity for submission of lower-cost alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of small businesses/small counties/small cities and mitigation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Before adopting/amending/repealing a rule, each agency shall consider the impact on small businesses, small counties, and small cities and, whenever practicable, shall tier rules to reduce disproportionate impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency may define size thresholds if necessary. Methods to reduce impact include: (I) less stringent compliance/reporting requirements; (II) less stringent schedules/deadlines; (III) consolidating/simplifying requirements; (IV) establishing performance standards or best management practices instead of design/operational standards; (V) exempting small entities from requirements. Agencies must consider these methods and implement feasible alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules ombudsman process and required responses
rubrics_metrics.description: If agency determines proposed action will affect small businesses, the agency shall send written notice of the rule to the rules ombudsman at least 28 days before the intended action. The agency shall adopt regulatory alternatives offered by the ombudsman that are feasible and consistent with objectives; if not adopting all alternatives, agency must file a detailed written statement explaining reasons and send a copy to the ombudsman within 3 working days after filing such notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatives offered by the ombudsman must be considered within prescribed timelines; failure to adopt all feasible alternatives requires formal written explanation filed and transmitted per statute. Adoption of alternatives can extend the 90-day filing period by 21 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearing rights and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the intended action concerns any rule other than one relating exclusively to procedure/practice, the agency shall, on request of any affected person received within 21 days after publication of the notice, give affected persons an opportunity to present evidence and argument on all issues; the agency may schedule a hearing and shall schedule one if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When hearings occur, staff must be available to explain and respond. If the agency head is a board/collegial body and hearings are requested, the board must conduct at least one hearing itself. Any material pertinent and submitted within 21 days after publication or between publication and final hearing will be considered and made part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to separate adjudicative proceeding when rulemaking inadequate
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking proceedings shall be governed solely by this section unless a person timely asserts that their substantial interests will be affected and affirmatively demonstrates the proceeding does not provide adequate opportunity to protect those interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If agency determines inadequacy, it shall suspend rulemaking and convene a separate proceeding under ss.120.569 and 120.57; similarly situated persons may be requested to join; upon conclusion, rulemaking resumes. This protects rights where rulemaking process cannot address individualized substantial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification and withdrawal procedures for proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: After final public hearing or after time for requesting a hearing has expired, if the rule is unchanged or contains only technical changes, the agency shall file a notice to that effect at least 7 days prior to filing for adoption. Any substantive change must be supported by the hearing record or be in response to timely written material or committee proposal; notices of change must be provided to requesters by certified mail or actual delivery no later than 21 days after the required notice and filed with the committee at least 21 days prior to filing for adoption. Agencies may withdraw proposed rules after notice and prior to adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of change must be published in the FAR at least 21 days prior to filing for adoption. Substantive changes require proper record support and timely notice; agencies may withdraw rules in whole or part after notice. After adoption and before effective date, rules may be modified/withdrawn only in limited circumstances (committee objection, final adverse order, failure to ratify by Legislature >90 days, pending committee consideration of an objection). Agencies must notify interested persons and Department of State when withdrawing/modifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing for final adoption and certification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If agency required to publish rules in FAC, upon approval of agency head it shall file with Department of State three certified copies of the rule, certified copies of any incorporated material, a summary of the rule, summary of hearings, and a detailed written statement of facts/circumstances justifying the rule. Agencies not required to publish file one certified copy and required materials in agency head office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rule may not be filed for adoption less than 28 days or more than 90 days after the notice, and various waiting periods apply (21 days after notice of change, 14 days after final public hearing, 21 days after SERC provided to those who submitted lower-cost alternatives, or until administrative law judge decision, whichever applies). Extensions to filing periods occur when notice of change or public hearing is published prior to expiration. If a petition for administrative determination is filed, filing period extends to 60 days after final order or judicial review. At filing time, agency must certify compliance with time limitations, statutory rulemaking requirements, and absence of pending administrative determinations. The committee certifies whether agency responded in writing to all material and timely written comments or inquiries. The Department shall reject rules not filed within prescribed time limits or not complying with statutory/rule requirements, including failure to respond to committee comments or inclusion of required SERC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and filing consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule shall be adopted on being filed with the Department of State and become effective 20 days after being filed, on a later date specified, on a date required by statute, or upon legislative ratification as required. Rules not required to be filed with the Department of State become effective when adopted by agency head or on later date specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the committee notifies an agency that an objection is being considered, the agency may postpone adoption to accommodate review; postponement tolls the 90-day filing period until committee completes review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rules: criteria, procedural protections, publication, and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency finds immediate danger to public health, safety, or welfare requires emergency action, it may adopt any rule necessitated by the immediate danger using any procedure fair under the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fair procedure must provide at least the procedural protections of statutes and Constitutions; agency must take only necessary action; agency must publish in writing specific facts/reasons for finding immediate danger and reasons concluding the procedure is fair. Notice of emergency rules (except certain local educational units) including full text must be published in first available issue of FAR and provided to the committee with any incorporated material. Emergency rules are judicially reviewable for findings. Emergency rules effective no more than 90 days and nonrenewable, except when agency has initiated non-emergency rulemaking addressing subject and (1) a challenge to proposed rules is filed and pending, or (2) proposed rules are awaiting legislative ratification. Emergency rules may become effective immediately on filing or on a date less than 20 days thereafter if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rules of procedure and required components
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administration Commission shall adopt uniform rules of procedure for agencies to comply with the requirements of this chapter; agencies must comply by specified date unless an exception is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform rules shall include procedures for scheduling public meetings/hearings/workshops; procedures for conducting meetings/hearings/workshops and taking evidence/testimony/argument in person and by communications media technology, affording equal consideration to all evidence regardless of communications method; rules on scheduling/access for communications media technology; rules for filing protests and formal written protests including prescribed bond forms; rules for filing petitions for administrative hearings requiring specific petition contents (identification, how/when notice was received, how substantial interests affected, disputed material facts, ultimate facts alleged, statutes/rules relied on, relief sought); rules for respondent requests for hearings in enforcement/disciplinary actions requiring specific contents; rules for petitions for declaratory statements describing contents of notices for publication in FAR and time limits for intervention/hearing petitions; requirement each agency head provide a description of agency organization and operations on its website; procedures for granting or denying variances and waivers under s.120.542. Exceptions to uniform rules may be petitioned and approved for specified reasons and, if approved, must be published and organized clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications media technology equality and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules must provide procedures for conducting public meetings/hearings/workshops and for taking evidence/testimony/argument in person and by means of communications media technology, and all evidence/testimony/argument shall be afforded equal consideration regardless of method of communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices for meetings/hearings/workshops using communications media technology must state how interested persons may attend and name locations where facilities will be available; limiting points of access to places not normally open to the public is presumed to violate right of access and make official action void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of petitions and forms for hearings, protests, and declaratory statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules shall require petitions for administrative hearings to include specified facts (petitioner identification, how/when notice received, impact on substantial interests, disputed facts, ultimate facts alleged, specific rules/statutes alleged to be violated, relief sought). Similar specific content requirements apply for respondent requests in enforcement actions and for petitions for declaratory statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may provide election-of-rights forms for respondents as long as forms only require the statutorily-specified information and do not add requirements unless authorized by law. Rules shall describe contents of notices for publication in FAR including time limits for intervention or filing for hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of federal standards: special procedure and objections
rubrics_metrics.description: In pursuing state implementation of federal programs, an agency may adopt rules substantively identical to federal regulations with special procedures: publish notice of intent at least 21 days prior to filing; provide notice to committee at least 21 days prior to filing; consider written comments received within 14 days after publication of notice of intent; rule adopted upon filing with Department of State; substantive changes from noticed rules require republishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules adopted under this subsection become effective on the date designated by the agency but not earlier than the federal regulation effective date. Any substantially affected person may file an objection within 14 days after publication specifying portions objected to and reasons; the agency shall not proceed to adopt objected portions under this subsection unless it deems the objection frivolous, though it may proceed under general rulemaking procedures (subsection (3)).
